title: The Best Luxury SUVs with 3 Rows in 2026
summary: Luxury three-row SUVs provide extra seating without sacrificing elegance or amenities. These are the CarGurus Editorial team's picks for vehicles that can transport multiple passengers in style.
body_text: Finding a luxury SUV that genuinely seats three rows of passengers—without sacrificing the refinement, technology, and driving experience that justify the premium price—is a narrower search than it might first appear. Many vehicles in this segment technically offer a third row, but the real-world usability of that space varies considerably from model to model. Some, like the Cadillac Escalade and Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class, are purpose-built for family hauling with adult-friendly rear seating and generous cargo room. Others, like the Genesis GV80 and Audi Q7, include a third row as more of an occasional-use option. Both have their merits. Beyond seating capacity, buyers in this segment are weighing a wide range of priorities: towing capability, fuel economy or electric range, off-road hardware, driver-assistance technology, and how well the infotainment system holds up in daily use. The Lexus GX, for instance, brings impressive towing numbers and a body-on-frame build, while the Lucid Gravity takes a completely different approach with an all-electric powertrain and up to an estimated 437 miles of range. The Range Rover and BMW X7 appeal to those who want a more driver-focused experience, while the Volvo XC90 and Mercedes-Benz GLS lean into comfort and safety credentials. This guide covers 10 of the best luxury SUVs with third-row seating currently available to help you find the right fit for your family and budget. What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different The Best Luxury SUVs with 3 Rows Audi Q7 Land Rover Range Rover Lexus GX Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class Volvo XC90 BMW X7 Cadillac Escalade Genesis GV80 Lucid Gravity Cadillac Vistiq FAQs Shopping Tools Related Topics 1. Audi Q7 CarGurus expert rating: 7.3 out of 10 CarGurus user rating: 4.7 out of 5 Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus: 35.3% Overall CarGurus rating: 4.6 out of 5 Pros Cons Stylish design Poor fuel economy Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto Cramped third row Standard all-wheel drive (AWD) Outdated advanced driver-assistance features For shoppers who want a luxury three-row SUV that prioritizes a premium feel and confident road manners, the refreshed 2025 Audi Q7 leans into what Audi does best: sharp design, a clean cabin layout, and standard AWD across the lineup. Power depends on trim, with a 2.0-liter turbo four-cylinder making 261 hp and 273 lb-ft of torque, or a 3.0-liter turbo V6 with 335 hp and 365 lb-ft of torque. The Q7 is polished and composed in daily driving, and it can feel surprisingly agile for a big family hauler—especially when equipped with available all-wheel steering. Where the Q7's three-row mission gets more complicated is in the way it uses its space. Audi says it seats seven, but the third row is best reserved for kids, and access back there can be awkward. Cargo room is also on the modest side for the class, with 14.2 cubic feet behind the third row, 35.7 cubic feet with it folded, and 69.6 cubic feet with both rear rows down. Tech is a strong point—wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, Google-based navigation, and an available 360-degree camera help day-to-day usability—but some driver-assistance features feel behind newer rivals, particularly lane-centering behavior. Pricing starts at $61,795 including destination and can climb quickly with options, so value-minded buyers will want to be careful about how they spec it. The CarGurus Verdict: "While the 2025 Audi Q7 has a lot going for it in terms of driving dynamics and engine prowess, it falls behind the competition when it comes to safety tech. Further, the third row is cramped for anyone but the smallest of humans, and the price can skyrocket as you move up the trim line." - Emme Hall Read our most recent Audi Q7 review Search for Audi Q7 See all 2021 Audi Q7 $29,216 57,468 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal San Antonio, TX 2023 Audi Q7 $28,145 62,914 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Harlingen, TX 2025 Audi Q7 $40,000 32,394 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Boulder, CO 2023 Audi Q7 $32,722 38,811 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Mckinney, TX 2022 Audi Q7 $33,992 20,412 miles No additional dealer fees Great Deal Sacramento, CA 2018 Audi Q7 $20,777 49,661 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Anacortes, WA 2. Land Rover Range Rover CarGurus expert rating: 7.7 out of 10 CarGurus user rating: 4.6 out of 5 Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus: 33.1% Overall CarGurus rating: 4.6 out of 5 Pros Cons Multiple powertrain options Unintuitive technology Stylish design Poor value for money Standard all-wheel drive For luxury-SUV shoppers who actually need three rows, the Range Rover's long-wheelbase configuration can be optioned with a third row, and for 2025 those three-row models are seven-seaters with second-row captain's chairs and a third-row bench. Headroom is generous across all three rows, and Land Rover makes third-row access less of a hassle with power-folding seats and conveniently placed controls. Among the vehicles in this guide, the Cadillac Escalade leads the pack with 121 cubic feet of total cargo space when both rear rows are folded, and 25.5 cubic feet behind the third row with all seats up. The BMW X7 is also competitive, offering 90.4 cubic feet with the second and third rows folded. At the other end of the spectrum, the Range Rover offers just 11 cubic feet behind its third row, and the Audi Q7 provides 14.2 cubic feet in the same configuration—so cargo capacity varies significantly across this segment and is worth checking carefully before you buy. Which luxury three-row SUVs offer the best towing capacity? If towing is a priority, the Lexus GX leads this group with a maximum towing capacity of up to 9,063 pounds. The Range Rover is close behind at 8,200 pounds, followed by the Cadillac Escalade at 7,900 pounds (with 4WD) and the BMW X7 at 7,500 pounds. The Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class is rated at 7,700 pounds, while the Genesis GV80 tops out at 6,000 pounds and the Cadillac Vistiq at 5,000 pounds. The Lucid Gravity's towing rating was not specified at publication time. Which luxury three-row SUVs have the most usable third rows for adults? Third-row usability varies considerably in this segment. The Cadillac Escalade, Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class, and Lucid Gravity are generally considered the most adult-friendly in terms of headroom and legroom in the third row. The Range Rover's long-wheelbase three-row configuration also offers generous headroom across all rows. By contrast, the Audi Q7, Volvo XC90, and Genesis GV80 have tighter third rows that are better suited to children or occasional short-trip use for adults. Are there any electric or plug-in hybrid options among luxury three-row SUVs? Yes. The Lucid Gravity is the only fully electric option in this guide, with an estimated range of up to 437 miles for three-row models. For plug-in hybrid options, the Range Rover offers a PHEV with an EPA-rated 53 miles of electric range, and the Volvo XC90 T8 provides up to 33 miles of electric range. The Cadillac Vistiq is also fully electric, with Cadillac estimating at least 300 miles of range. The remaining models—Audi Q7, Lexus GX, Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class, BMW X7, Cadillac Escalade, and Genesis GV80—are conventional gasoline-powered vehicles, though several use mild-hybrid systems to improve efficiency. Which luxury three-row SUVs offer hands-free highway driving? Hands-free highway driving is available on a select few models in this segment. The Cadillac Escalade includes Super Cruise as standard equipment, making it one of the more accessible options for this feature. The Lucid Gravity offers hands-free highway driving as an available upgrade through its DreamDrive system. The Genesis GV80 includes standard Highway Drive Assist, though it is not a fully hands-free system. The BMW X7 requires the Driving Assistance Professional Package for its Highway Assistant feature. The Audi Q7, Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class, Volvo XC90, and Range Rover do not currently offer a hands-free highway driving system. What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different? Most car-shopping websites publish lists of the best cars across a variety of categories, with recommendations generally driven by editorial expertise. title: A Letter from Chris Geoghegan on Joining Ashby
summary: Building people software for high growth companies.
body_text: I spent over a decade leading Product at Zapier. I'm not one to jump around between jobs, so when I decided it was time for something new, it had to be a company I could bet on for the long term. For me, that bet is Ashby, and I wanted to share more on why I'm making this my next long-term home. I first came to Ashby as a customer and a user. As a functional leader, one of my responsibilities is to attract top product talent. I spend time reviewing candidates and inspecting interview loops. Ashby made that feel effortless and enjoyable. I remember thinking: The people behind this understand recruiting. So when the opportunity to speak with Benji came up, I jumped at it. It didn't take long to realize the excellent product was no accident. Behind the scenes I discovered a robust platform, a deliberate culture, and a massive vision. I wanted to be a part of it. 1. An Enduring Foundation It's rare to find HR software that is a joy to use. With Ashby it's different. The care and craft the team has for building software comes through. Many startups scramble to get any sense of product-market fit. Benji and Abhik had a clear vision for what they wanted to build. This allowed them to invest in building an enduring foundation for an ATS with the best analytics on the market. This foundation is also what enables the team to deliver and move as fast as they do. In the future, it's what will enable us to build and launch valuable new products for customers. It shows in the results too. The fastest-growing companies in the world already depend on Ashby . 2. An Empowered Team In each conversation I had with an Ashby PM or engineer, it was clear the team owned delivery end-to-end. This is possible because Ashby recruits a team that is full-stack and multi-talented. Individuals spend less time in meetings and Slack . They spend more time delivering great software. As I spent time with Benji, I felt a strong sense of alignment about how great products actually get built. By individuals who understand customer problems and own the solutions end-to-end. And the proof is in the velocity. The output velocity given the team size is impressive. 3. A Unique Vision As I went through the interview process, I also uncovered an exciting vision beyond what is seen publicly. Today, Ashby is the best all-in-one recruiting software. For People and HR functions, the center of gravity is shifting away from being highly administrative functions and toward being the locus of talent attraction and retention. The vast majority of existing tools silo data, don't scale, or feel like a burden to use. I'm excited to work with the team to expand this platform. To solve more talent-centered problems for the fastest growing companies. To build people software the people love to use. What I'll Be Focused On I'm joining a team that's already shipping at a high level. This means my first job is to build deep context on our product, customers, and team. Next, I'll focus on improving how we operate as a product team. I'll help scale what's already working, grow the talent on our team, and drive consistent high-quality delivery. Over time, as I build up the necessary context, I'm excited to help shape the long term direction of Ashby and expand the product and platform. This feels like a pivotal moment for Ashby and I'm excited to be stepping into this role. The foundation is strong, the team is sharp, and the opportunity ahead of us is massive. I'm looking forward to building with this team for years to come. And I’d love for more people to join us. Explore our open roles today .

"The long-term outlook for semiconductor manufacturing remains compelling as AI continues to drive investment across the industry. Our priority is executing UCT 3.0 by expanding our global manufacturing capacity, enhancing engineering and operational capabilities, and accelerating digital transformation. Together, these initiatives position us to support our customers with greater speed, agility, and scale while delivering sustainable, profitable growth and creating long-term value for our shareholders." Second Quarter 2026 GAAP Financial Results Total revenue was $644.9 million. Products contributed $572.7 million and Services added $72.2 million. Total gross margin was 16.1%, operating margin was 4.6%, and net income was $8.7 million or $0.19 per diluted share. This compares to total revenue of $533.7 million, gross margin of 15.8%, operating margin of 2.1%, and net loss of $(17.9) million or $(0.40) per diluted share, in the prior quarter. Second Quarter 2026 Non-GAAP Financial Results On a non-GAAP basis, gross margin was 16.7%, operating margin was 7.0%, and net income was $32.3 million or $0.70 per diluted share. This compares to gross margin of 16.5%, operating margin of 5.1%, and net income of $14.5 million or $0.31 per diluted share in the prior quarter. Third Quarter 2026 Outlook The Company expects revenue in the range of $700 million to $750 million. The Company expects GAAP diluted net income per share to be between $0.67 and $0.87 and non-GAAP diluted net income per share to be between $0.83 and $1.03. The Webcast will be available on the Investor Relations section of the Company's website at http://uct.com/investors/events/ . About Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. is a leading developer and supplier of critical subsystems, components, parts, and ultra-high purity cleaning and analytical services, primarily for the semiconductor industry. Under its Products division, UCT offers its customers an integrated outsourced solution for major subassemblies, improved design-to-delivery cycle times, design for manufacturability, prototyping, and high-precision manufacturing. Under its Services Division, UCT offers its customers tool chamber parts cleaning and coating, as well as micro-contamination analytical services. Ultra Clean is headquartered in Hayward, California. Additional information is available at www.uct.com . title: 25 Reasons to Learn Spanish for Travel, Work, and Life
summary: Spanish is spoken by over 500 million people across more than 20 countries, making it one of the most practical languages to pick up for travel, work, and every…
body_text: Spanish is spoken by over 500 million people across more than 20 countries, making it one of the most practical languages to pick up for travel, work, and everyday connection. Whether the goal is navigating a trip through Latin America, communicating with Spanish-speaking colleagues, or simply understanding a favorite song, the reasons to learn Spanish are concrete and immediate. Finding the best way to learn conversational Spanish comes down to practicing the way people actually speak, not just how the language appears on a page. Most traditional methods focus on grammar rules and written exercises, which rarely translate into confident real-world conversations. Parrot takes a different approach by centering practice on natural, spoken Spanish from the start. For anyone ready to move beyond textbooks and actually hold a conversation, learn Spanish . Table of Contents Why More People Than Ever Are Learning Spanish 25 Reasons to Learn Spanish Why Many People Never Reach Conversational Spanish How to Learn Spanish in a Way You Can Actually Sustain Is Learning Spanish Worth It for Your Goals? How Parrot Makes Learning Spanish Easier to Stick With Start Learning Spanish Today Summary Conversational Spanish fluency requires far more time than most learners expect. Research cited by the HelloTalk Blog estimates that English speakers need roughly 600 to 750 hours of study to reach conversational ability in Spanish. That figure reframes the challenge from a weekend project into a long-term commitment that demands a sustainable method, not just motivation. Inconsistency is the most common reason learners stall before reaching fluency. Only 1 in 5 language learners ever reach conversational fluency according to the HelloTalk Blog, and irregular practice is one of the clearest contributing factors. Missing a few weeks creates a psychological gap that pushes many learners to quit entirely, even when their foundational progress was solid. Spanish is growing faster than most people realize, and the demand is coming from real economic and social shifts. The number of Spanish speakers worldwide grew by 30 million in 2025 alone, a 5% increase in a single year according to Language Magazine. Supply chains across Latin America, bilingual urban neighborhoods, and expanding Spanish-language media are all driving that growth from the ground up. The financial case for Spanish fluency is real, though it varies by industry. Bilingual employees in healthcare, education, customer service, and finance are in consistent short supply relative to demand, and in sectors with high Spanish-speaking customer volume the wage premium is measurable. Beyond earnings, fluency makes workers genuinely harder to replace in client-facing roles where communication quality directly affects outcomes. Enjoyment is not a reward for serious learners. It is the actual mechanism that sustains long-term progress. A 2024 systematic review published in Frontiers in Education found that emotionally engaging learning experiences consistently improved motivation and sustained participation, but only when they supported meaningful language use rather than streaks or point systems. Learners who quit overwhelmingly built routines around obligation rather than genuine interest. The personal reasons to learn Spanish tend to outlast the professional ones. Sitting at a family dinner and understanding the conversation in real time, laughing at a joke without waiting for someone to explain it, or expressing something personal to someone who matters to you in their own language- these moments don't appear on a resume but consistently drive long-term commitment in ways that career goals alone rarely do. Parrot's Learn Spanish app addresses the consistency and method gap directly by delivering short-form authentic video content built around comprehensible input, so daily practice fits inside a real schedule rather than requiring a cleared calendar. Why More People Than Ever Are Learning Spanish Spanish is growing faster than most people realize . Language Magazine reports that Spanish speakers worldwide grew by 30 million in 2025 alone , representing a 5% increase in one year . This is not gradual drift but a measurable surge in global demand for the language. "Spanish speakers worldwide grew by 30 million in 2025 alone — a 5% increase in a single year." — Language Magazine / Observatorio del Español, 2025 🔑 Takeaway: A 5% single-year growth rate across a language spoken by hundreds of millions is extraordinary . This is momentum at scale , signaling that learning Spanish is becoming less a personal enrichment choice and more a practical necessity . The growth reflects real, structural changes in how people live and work , not a passing trend. Supply chains stretch across Latin America . Streaming platforms serve Spanish-language audiences in every time zone . Neighborhoods in cities like Houston , Miami , and Los Angeles have become bilingual environments. Spanish is expanding because the world people live in needs it. 💡 Tip: If you are deciding when to start learning Spanish, the answer is now : the economic, cultural, and social demand for Spanish speakers is accelerating . ⚠️ Warning: Treating Spanish as a "nice to have" skill is an increasingly costly mistake . In bilingual job markets like Miami or Los Angeles, Spanish fluency is becoming a baseline expectation , not a bonus. What's really driving people to learn Spanish now? The economic case is compelling, but the more honest reason people learn Spanish is personal. They want to talk to a partner's family without a translator. They want to laugh at a joke in real time. Language fluency at that level is a social skill, and the gap shows up in the smallest, most human moments. According to Speakeasy BCN , Spanish is the second most spoken language by native speakers. This scale means the return on modest fluency is unusually high. Ten minutes of real practice compounds differently than ten minutes of vocabulary flashcards: one builds pattern recognition , the other builds a list you'll forget by Thursday. Why do so many learners stall before fluency clicks? Most people who want to learn Spanish have already tried apps with streaks and cartoon owls, or bought textbooks that taught the subjunctive before ordering coffee. The frustration isn't a lack of effort—it's a mismatch between method and goal. Learners who want real conversations need to hear real Spanish, not drill conjugation tables alone. Tools like Parrot use short-form video immersion built around comprehensible input, helping learners build fluency through natural exposure rather than memorization. The barrier to starting isn't time or talent: it's the belief that fluency requires years of formal study before anything clicks. That belief is wrong, and the data behind Spanish's explosive growth suggests millions of people are already figuring that out. Being truly fluent in Spanish opens doors that most other language skills simply can't. "Spanish is the official language of 21 countries and is spoken by over 500 million native speakers around the world." — Middlebury Language Schools Spanish is one of the world's most widely spoken languages, with a broad global presence: Official countries – Spanish is an official language in 21 countries around the world. Native speakers – More than 500 million people speak Spanish as their first language. Global reach – It is one of the most widely spoken and influential languages worldwide, used across multiple continents. 🎯 Key Point: With 500 million+ native speakers across 21 countries , Spanish is one of the most powerful language investments you can make — unlocking career opportunities , travel experiences , and cultural connections that few other skills can match. 💡 Tip: You don't need to be perfectly fluent to start reaping the real-world benefits of Spanish — even basic conversational skills can dramatically expand your personal and professional world . Career and Business 1. Access More Job Opportunities Bilingual employees in healthcare, education, customer service, and finance are scarce relative to employer demand. Employers across English-speaking countries consistently list Spanish as the most requested second language in job postings, particularly in roles where direct customer communication affects outcomes. 2. Stand Out to Employers Speaking Spanish demonstrates persistence through difficulty, adaptability to new situations, and cross-cultural communication—skills valued in job performance and advancement, not merely on resumes. 3. Serve Spanish-Speaking Customers More Effectively When a patient cannot explain their symptoms or a customer cannot understand a policy, everyone loses. Speaking Spanish removes that friction and builds trust that no translation app can replicate. 4. Expand International Business Opportunities Talking directly with partners, suppliers, and clients across Latin America and Spain builds relationships that eliminate intermediaries. Misunderstandings that cost deals often stem from language gaps . 5. Increase Your Earning Potential The wage premium for bilingual workers varies by industry and location, but in sectors with high Spanish-speaking customer volume , the advantage is clear and measurable. You become irreplaceable in such roles. Travel and Living Abroad 6. Travel More Confidently Translation apps fail in loud markets, on fast-moving buses, or when someone speaks quickly and informally. Knowing Spanish lets you navigate those moments with confidence. 7. Connect With Locals Instead of Staying in Tourist Areas The best meal in Mexico City won't be on an English menu. The most honest travel advice in Colombia won't come from a hotel concierge. Language gets you past the surface. 8. Navigate Everyday Situations More Easily Shopping, using public transit, visiting a pharmacy, or sorting out a billing issue becomes less stressful when you understand what's being said . Fluency is the difference between feeling capable and feeling helpless. 9. Prepare for Studying or Living Abroad Arriving in a Spanish-speaking country without the language means spending your first months isolated. Learning before you go shortens that adjustment period and lets you live where you are instead of merely getting by. 10. Enjoy More Authentic Travel Experiences Humor, local history, and cultural nuance rarely survive translation. Understanding a joke in context or catching a regional expression creates a different quality of experience than reading subtitles. Culture and Entertainment 11. Watch Spanish Films and Series Without Subtitles Subtitles divide your attention between reading and watching. Spanish cinema and television, from Pedro Almodóvar's films to Colombian crime dramas, reward viewers who follow dialogue directly. 12. Understand Spanish Music and Lyrics Artists like Bad Bunny, Rosalía, and Juanes tell stories, reference history, and play with language in ways that don't survive translation . The meaning lives in the original words. 13. Read Books in Their Original Language Gabriel García Márquez said translation is like looking at a tapestry from the back. Reading "Cien Años de Soledad" in Spanish differs fundamentally from any English version. 14. Follow Spanish Creators Across Digital Platforms Spanish-language content on YouTube, TikTok, and podcasts grows faster than most English-language categories. Learning Spanish grants access to millions of creators in education, comedy, fitness, and technology beyond the reach of English-only audiences. 15. Experience Different Cultures Through Language Language shapes how people express time, emotion, obligation, and relationships. Spanish has grammar structures and vocabulary that reflect a worldview English doesn't fully capture. Learning those structures changes how you think, not how you speak. Relationships and Community 16. Communicate With a Partner's Family Sitting at a dinner table and understanding the conversation, laughing at the right moment, asking a question that lands—that's belonging. Most people who start learning Spanish for work stay motivated because of moments like this. The relationship goal outlasts the resume goal almost every time. 17. Build Friendships Across Cultures Speaking someone's native language is an act of respect that transforms the relationship from polite tolerance to genuine connection. 18. Connect With Millions of Spanish Speakers Online Spanish is one of the most active languages across social platforms, gaming communities, and discussion forums. Fluency in Spanish opens access to communities that English-only users cannot reach. 19. Participate More Fully in Bilingual Communities Whether you live in Miami, Los Angeles, New York, or London, Spanish-speaking communities are part of daily life. Speaking their language with neighbors, local organizations, and at community events changes how you feel about where you live. 20. Develop Greater Cultural Empathy Learning another language forces you to hold two systems of meaning at once. This cognitive flexibility makes people better listeners, more patient communicators, and more aware of how context shapes meaning: a measurable shift in how you process other people. Personal Growth 21. Improve Memory and Cognitive Flexibility Managing two languages trains the brain to switch between competing systems, strengthening attention, working memory , and mental flexibility. This benefit extends to tasks unrelated to language. 22. Exercise Your Brain Throughout Life Learning a language over a long time is one of the few activities that challenges your brain and sustains engagement for years without feeling like work, especially when it fits naturally into your daily life. Research consistently supports the relationship between lifelong bilingualism and cognitive reserve . Most people think brain training requires dedicated effort and structured time. In reality, 10 to 15 minutes of genuine immersion in Spanish content, done consistently, produces more cognitive engagement than most formal study sessions twice as long. 23. Build Confidence by Learning a New Skill The first time you have a real conversation in Spanish, something changes. You prove to yourself that something you thought impossible is possible. That confidence tends to transfer . The common pattern with language learners who quit is that they never had that first real conversation. They studied vocabulary and grammar rules but never used language in practice. Methods built around comprehensible input , like short-form immersive video content, help learners reach that moment faster. Parrot uses scroll-friendly video immersion to make that first real conversation feel closer than most learners expect. 24. Gain Access to One of the World's Most Widely Spoken Languages According to the Instituto Cervantes, Spanish is spoken by more than 630 million people worldwide, making it one of the most powerful global languages for communication, business, travel, and culture. That reach means learning Spanish pays off across every area of life. 25. Open Doors to Learning Other Romance Languages Spanish shares deep structural and vocabulary roots with Portuguese, Italian, French, and Romanian. Learners who reach conversational Spanish consistently report that learning other Romance languages feels significantly more accessible because the cognitive framework is already in place. One language learned well becomes the foundation for several others. But knowing why to learn Spanish and reaching fluency are two different things, and the gap between them is where most people disappear. Why Many People Never Reach Conversational Spanish Most learners don't fail Spanish because they lack intelligence or commitment . They fail because the gap between starting and speaking fluently is wider than anyone warned them about , and the methods they're using weren't designed to close it. "The problem isn't the learner — it's the mismatch between expectations and reality that causes most people to quit before they get close." ⚠️ Warning: Motivation alone won't carry you to fluency. Without the right method , even the most dedicated learners hit a wall and never break through. According to the HelloTalk Blog , it takes English speakers roughly 600 to 750 hours of study to reach conversational Spanish . Most people treat it like a weekend project when it's actually more like a marathon with no finish line visible from the starting block. Regardless of the learning style, reaching Spanish proficiency requires a substantial time investment: Weekend project – May seem like a low-effort approach, but still requires approximately 600–750 hours of meaningful practice. Casual app use – Feels very low effort, yet achieving proficiency still demands around 600–750 hours of consistent learning. Structured marathon – Sets realistic expectations by recognising that reaching proficiency typically requires 600–750 hours of focused study and practice. 🔑 Takeaway: 600 to 750 hours is not a weekend commitment — it's the equivalent of working a full-time job for 4+ months straight . Treating it as anything less is the single biggest reason learners plateau and quit. Why does inconsistency stop so many learners in their tracks? The failure point is usually consistency, not capability. Missing three weeks of practice because life got busy, the app stopped feeling rewarding, or progress felt invisible creates a psychological gap that's hard to close. The HelloTalk Blog reports that only 1 in 5 language learners reach conversational fluency, with inconsistency being one of the clearest reasons why. Why do common study habits build recognition instead of real communication? Most people spend their early months memorizing vocabulary lists, doing grammar exercises, and collecting streaks on gamified apps. Those activities feel productive but build recognition, not communication. When a native speaker talks at natural speed with contractions and slang, that carefully memorized vocabulary often disappears under pressure. Apps like Parrot use short-form video immersion built on comprehensible input, helping learners encounter Spanish the way the brain absorbs language: through meaningful, contextual exposure rather than isolated drilling. Why does waiting to feel ready keep learners from actually speaking? Waiting to speak is another quiet trap. Many learners convince themselves they need to feel "ready" before attempting real conversation, but readiness built from study alone rarely arrives. Speaking activates a different thinking process than reading or listening. Those uncomfortable moments are not signs of failure; they are how passive knowledge becomes active fluency. What does a method actually optimized for conversational fluency look like? The problem isn't the learner. The methods most people use by default were never designed to develop conversation skills . They were designed to hit completion goals, keep people using the app, and create the feeling of progress. Real language learning requires repeated exposure to meaningful language, low-pressure practice, and enough enjoyment to sustain the habit long after initial motivation fades. Sustainable learning doesn't need more time. It needs a different relationship with the process itself. How to Learn Spanish in a Way You Can Actually Sustain Sustainable learning is a structured problem, not willpower . Learners who reach conversational fluency aren't those who studied hardest in January—they're those who built a routine that survived February, March, and every distracted Tuesday after that. "The learners who win aren't the most motivated — they're the most consistent ." — Language Acquisition Research 💡 Tip: Before picking an app or course, design your routine first . A 5-minute daily habit you actually keep beats a 2-hour session you abandon by week two. ⚠️ Warning: Relying on willpower alone is the #1 reason learners plateau. Structure —not motivation—keeps you moving forward. The critical difference between progress and plateau is rarely ability. It's contact time with the language , accumulated over weeks and months . According to the Amauta Spanish School Blog , Spanish has over 500 million native speakers worldwide. This abundance means podcasts, short videos, music, interviews, and storytelling in Spanish are everywhere —your biggest structural advantage as a learner. "Spanish has over 500 million native speakers worldwide, making authentic input infinitely accessible to learners at every level." — Amauta Spanish School Blog Different types of language input develop different skills while requiring varying levels of effort: Podcasts – Best for improving listening comprehension with relatively low effort. Short videos – Combine visual and audio learning, making them effective with low to moderate effort. Music – Reinforces vocabulary, pronunciation, and rhythm with very little effort. Interviews – Expose learners to natural speech patterns and conversational language, requiring moderate focus. Storytelling – Teaches grammar and vocabulary in context while developing deeper comprehension, typically requiring moderate to high effort. 🎯 Key Point: With 500 million+ native speakers , the real barrier to Spanish fluency isn't access to content — it's building the consistent structure to consume it. What a sustainable routine actually looks like Four or five short structured sessions weekly build your grammatical foundation. Daily listening—even 20 minutes of Spanish video or audio at your level—trains your brain to recognize rhythm and sentence patterns before you consciously understand every word. Two or three speaking sessions each week, whether with a tutor, language partner, or talking through your day aloud in Spanish, convert passive recognition into active communication. Most learners skip speaking because it feels uncomfortable. That discomfort is where fluency lives. How do you close the gap between intention and automatic habit? The friction point is the gap between "I'll do it later" and a habit that runs on autopilot. Apps like Parrot address this by delivering short-form immersive video content built around comprehensible input, allowing learners to get authentic Spanish exposure in 10- to 15-minute scroll-friendly sessions that fit into a real day rather than requiring a cleared calendar. Why enjoyment isn't optional Enjoyment isn't a reward for serious learners—it's how learning works. A 2024 systematic review in Frontiers in Education found that emotionally connected learning experiences consistently improved motivation and sustained participation when they supported real language use rather than rewarding streaks or points. Watching a travel documentary in Spanish because you want to visit Colombia isn't a shortcut; it's the most direct path to the repeated, meaningful exposure that builds fluency. Follow the football club. Watch the cooking channel. Read about the music. The content you consume in Spanish should feel like something you'd seek out anyway. What actually causes learners to quit? Students who quit aren't the ones who lacked discipline. They're the ones who built routines around obligation instead of interest and eventually ran out of willpower to sustain them. Willpower runs out. Curiosity doesn't. But knowing how to structure your learning is only part of the picture. The more personal question is whether Spanish fluency is worth pursuing for your current situation. Is Learning Spanish Worth It for Your Goals? Whether Spanish is worth learning comes down to a simple test: does the life you want require it, or would it improve it? For most people , the answer is yes , but the reasons are more personal than expected. "The question isn't whether Spanish has value — it's whether your goals make that value impossible to ignore ." 🎯 Key Point: The real ROI of learning Spanish isn't universal; it's defined by your career ambitions, travel goals, and personal connections. 💡 Tip: Before committing to a Spanish learning plan , ask yourself one question: would fluency open a door you want to walk through? If yes, the investment is almost always worth it . The value of learning Spanish depends on how it aligns with your personal or professional goals: Career in global business – Spanish can have a high impact by expanding communication opportunities in international markets. Travel to Latin America or Spain – Speaking Spanish makes travel easier and enables richer cultural experiences. Connecting with Spanish-speaking family – Learning the language can strengthen personal relationships and cultural connections. Cognitive and brain health benefits – Learning a second language is associated with cognitive benefits such as improved attention, memory, and mental flexibility. Casual hobby with no clear use case – Learning Spanish can still be enjoyable, but the urgency and long-term motivation may be lower without a specific goal. ⚠️ Warning: Skipping the goal-alignment step is the most common reason learners quit — they start without a personal reason strong enough to sustain the effort. What practical benefits does learning Spanish actually open up? The practical case is hard to ignore. According to the HelloTalk Blog , Spanish is the second most spoken language in the world by native speakers. Travel becomes richer, professional doors open faster, and cultural access—from literature to film to music—is immediate and lasting. What actually keeps learners motivated over the long term? But the most lasting motivation isn't career advantage or travel convenience. It's the irreplaceable moments: speaking directly with a partner's family without a translator, having a real conversation with a friend who grew up speaking Spanish at home, expressing something personal in the right words to someone who matters. Those moments don't appear on a resume, but they stay with you. Learners who persist with Spanish typically had a specific person or place they wanted to reach, not abstract fluency. The familiar approach of downloading an app, building a streak, and trusting points becomes language work initially. But the habit of learning and the habit of checking in aren't the same, and many learners notice the gap between daily activity and actual progress. Apps like Parrot use short-form video immersion and comprehensible input so that 10 to 15 minutes of daily practice builds real conversational ability rather than maintaining a number on a screen. How far do you actually need to go to reach your goal? How far you need to go depends entirely on your goal. If you want basic conversations while traveling through a country where Spanish is an official language in 20 or more countries , a few months of consistent practice suffices. If you want to work in Spanish, study abroad, or integrate into a Spanish-speaking community, you're looking at a longer journey, though still achievable. The barrier to starting is lower than most people assume. Spanish justifies itself the first time you understand something you weren't supposed to, or say something in Spanish and watch someone's face change because they weren't expecting you to meet them there. That moment is the return on investment no spreadsheet captures. title: July Product Pulse: Less Busywork Before, During, and After Every Event | Zuddl Blog
summary: Zuddl's July updates take three recurring workarounds off your plate - the manual Salesforce campaign, the video editor for speaker clips, and the CSM request before every event - plus five more improvements across lead capture, accessibility, and checkout.
body_text: Salesforce Campaigns That Create Themselves You create an event in Zuddl. Then you open Salesforce, create a campaign, name it to match whatever format you agreed on three quarters ago, set the status to Planned, enter the dates, and link it back to the event. Skip this step and no registration data flows to your CRM. Do it for 30 events a quarter and it's the kind of task nobody owns but everybody notices when it slips. After one setup at the org level, every new or duplicated event gets its own correctly-named Salesforce campaign the moment you create it. Registration data flows to your CRM without anyone remembering to link things up. Manual campaign IDs still work whenever you need them. Configure Lead Enrichment Without a Support Ticket You have an API kit from Maritz or Cvent. You've used it at every conference. But every event, you send those details to the CSM and wait for them to configure it, and hope it's done before your reps start scanning. Now you submit it yourself from the Lead Capture App settings. Once connected, your badge provider becomes an enrichment source alongside Zuddl's own. You choose which gets priority and which is the fallback. If your primary source returns full data, your reps see that. If it comes back thin, the fallback fills the gaps. Every Speaker Gets Their Own Recording Your keynote ended two hours ago. Marketing needs a 90-second clip of the CEO's closing remarks for LinkedIn by Friday. Your options: send the full-mix recording to a video editor and wait, or scrub through the timeline yourself and hope the export settings are right. Your content team can now grab individual speaker clips straight from the Recording Library. Each speaker gets their own audio-video file, and screen shares are captured separately. Pull what you need and start repurposing into social clips, podcast segments, or highlight reels. No editor in the loop. One-time enablement through your CSM. Applies to every webinar and virtual session from there. Documentation: Events | Webinars Enhancements Pre-upload Event Attendees for Context at the Booth Reps at third-party booths scan badges with no context on who's a target account. Upload your attendee list before the show. Scanned badges auto-match during lead capture, surfacing enriched contact data at the point of scan. No match, the lead is captured as new. Closed Captions on Every On-Demand Recording Live sessions had captions. On-demand recordings didn't. The same CC toggle now covers both, with captions auto-translating into up to 6 target languages. Attendees switch languages or turn captions off directly from the player. Connect with Any Attendee in One QR Scan Attendees scan each other's QR codes in the Zuddl Events App to connect on the spot. Faster than spelling out a name or swapping business cards. One scan opens the other attendee's full profile. On by default. Export Badge Photos Directly from the App Badge photos from lead scanning were stuck in the app with no way to get them out. Reps can now export them from the Lead Capture app, one at a time or in bulk. All scans are grouped by time for easy review. Automated Tax Calculation at Checkout Tax rates used to be looked up manually and applied per ticket, per jurisdiction, per event. Zuddl now integrates with Avalara to calculate the right tax automatically at checkout. Every invoice and transaction reflects the correct amount, with one-time setup at the org level. title: Securing the Infrastructure of Intelligence
summary: Land, Power and Shell: The Next Critical Resource for AI factories.
body_text: AI factories are the defining infrastructure of the AI era — where compute transforms energy and data into intelligence that powers every business, industry and country. In the AI economy, compute is revenue. AI factories require a full stack of critical resources: advanced chips, packaging, memory, and networking — as well as land, power and shell. Just as NVIDIA has used its scale, long-term visibility and supply-chain partnerships to secure critical semiconductor resources, we are now applying that same discipline to secure LPS capacity exclusively for NVIDIA AI factories. Today, we are partnering with SB Energy to secure LPS capacity at the exceptional PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Portsmouth, Ohio, to host NVIDIA compute. OpenAI will be the tenant. LPS: The Next Strategic Resource For the vast majority of NVIDIA customers, securing LPS has long been a part of their infrastructure strategy. The world’s largest cloud service providers and investment-grade enterprises have balance sheets, infrastructure expertise, and long-term contracts to secure LPS independently. They build and operate AI factories using NVIDIA accelerated computing, networking, systems and software. This model will continue to represent most of NVIDIA’s business. But frontier AI labs are different. Frontier AI labs have extraordinary demand for training and inference compute, but many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support. They may have strong customer demand and rapidly growing revenue yet still lack the decades-long infrastructure contracts and investment-grade financing capacity needed to secure the AI factory infrastructure independently. Their growth is increasingly constrained not by algorithms or customer demand, but by the availability of compute. For these companies, more compute means more intelligence, more products, more users and more revenue. NVIDIA is helping provide the infrastructure that powers this flywheel. PORTS-Pike: A Site for Generations of NVIDIA Compute OpenAI will build and operate a world-class AI factory at PORTS-Pike. The AI factory will use NVIDIA’s full-stack DSX AI factory platform, including GPUs, CPUs, networking, and infrastructure software. The initial deployment is expected to provide 4.25 gigawatts of AI factory capacity. Each generation of NVIDIA AI factory systems deployed at PORTS-Pike could represent approximately 1.5 million NVIDIA GPUs, or approximately $150 billion to $200 billion in NVIDIA revenue. Over 20 years, the site can support multiple upgrade cycles. This is the essential economic point: the LPS commitment secures a long-lived AI factory site, while the NVIDIA compute inside can be upgraded repeatedly. Each new generation can deliver greater production, more intelligence and better economics. NVIDIA may also choose to extend the arrangement at PORTS-Pike beyond the initial 4.25 gigawatts to secure the remaining capacity of 3.75 gigawatts. OpenAI and NVIDIA Expanding Compute Opportunity More broadly, OpenAI has committed to substantial deployments of NVIDIA AI infrastructure through 2030. OpenAI’s existing and planned commitments represent approximately 12 gigawatts of NVIDIA compute, with an opportunity to expand to approximately 16 gigawatts if NVIDIA extends the PORTS-Pike arrangement beyond the initial 4.25 gigawatts. At these levels, the opportunity represents roughly $600 billion of NVIDIA compute through 2030. The Important Questions What is NVIDIA guaranteeing, and for how long? NVIDIA is supporting the LPS infrastructure at PORTS-Pike for approximately 4 gigawatts over a 20-year term, securing a site on which NVIDIA compute will be exclusively deployed. Our support is limited to defined portions of lease and power payments, along with a specified residual-value commitment — not the full cost of the site or all of the tenant’s obligations. The guarantee will become effective in phases as data centers are placed in service between 2028 and 2030. As OpenAI makes lease payments and capacity comes online, NVIDIA’s remaining exposure declines. Why is NVIDIA guaranteeing PORTS-Pike? LPS has become a critical constraint on AI factory deployment. NVIDIA is selectively securing exceptional sites where we can host multiple generations of NVIDIA compute and serve durable customer demand. The productive life of the site extends through multiple generations of NVIDIA systems, each capable of producing more intelligence and more revenue than the generation before. Is this circular financing? No. OpenAI will pay the lease. NVIDIA uses its scale and long-term visibility to secure PORTS-Pike to host NVIDIA compute. This is the same discipline we apply to supply-chain management: we secure critical inputs when we have visibility into customer demand and when doing so enables long-term productive capacity. What happens to PORTS-Pike if OpenAI does not use the site in the future? NVIDIA compute is versatile, fungible and broadly adopted. The capacity can be resold to another qualified tenant across NVIDIA’s global ecosystem of cloud service providers, enterprises, AI labs and startups. CUDA makes NVIDIA compute more than hardware. It gives developers and NVIDIA engineers a common platform to continually improve installed systems. CUDA makes NVIDIA compute versatile. Versatility makes it fungible. Fungibility drives utilization and durability — making NVIDIA compute a productive asset: rentable and financeable. The value of an exceptional site, like PORTS-Pike, is not limited to one customer or one generation of compute. NVIDIA’s standardized platform, broad developer ecosystem and large market of potential users support the ability to redeploy productive capacity over time. How much LPS will NVIDIA secure? It will be strategic and disciplined. Most NVIDIA customers will continue to secure their own LPS. The vast majority of LPS hosting NVIDIA compute will continue to be secured directly by CSPs, enterprises, sovereign AI builders and other customers. NVIDIA will focus selectively on exceptional sites where visible, durable demand can support multiple generations of NVIDIA compute. The Infrastructure of Intelligence PORTS-Pike represents the next step in NVIDIA’s journey. We began by building accelerated computing chips. We then expanded to systems, networking, CUDA and full-stack AI factories. Today, we are helping secure the critical infrastructure required to build these factories. NVIDIA is the full-stack AI infrastructure platform. We are investing in the long-lived foundations of AI factories so our customers can deploy the most productive compute platform in the world, generation after generation. By securing the critical resources needed to host NVIDIA compute, we can help the world’s most innovative companies build the AI factories that will power the age of intelligence.

body_text: View All News Twenty One Capital Issues Letter from CEO, Raphael Zagury August 11, 2026 Download (opens in new window) AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Twenty One Capital, Inc. (“Twenty One” or “XXI” or the “Company”) (NYSE: XXI) today published a letter from the Company's Chief Executive Officer, Raphael Zagury. Dear Shareholders, Today we released our second-quarter results. And while I encourage you to take a look at our latest 10-Q filing to learn about what happened during the quarter, this letter to shareholders speaks to something more fundamental about the company I now lead as CEO: what you own, why it matters, and what we intend to do to improve operational opportunities and increase shareholder value. Many of you reached out over the past few weeks with questions. Some were about the company. Others were about Bitcoin itself. To answer them properly, I should probably start with why I am here. Growing up in Brazil, I watched my mother race through a grocery store because prices could change more than once a day. I learned early on what broken money does to families, and I have dedicated my life’s work to solving that issue ever since. That is the short answer as to why I took this job. The longer answer is addressed in this letter. Twenty One owns one of the largest Bitcoin balance sheets in the public markets. That is a real advantage, but if Twenty One is going to be worth owning, it must become more than a Bitcoin treasury. In the year ahead, I plan on leading Twenty One with a focus on five priorities: First, finishing the corporate foundation: governance, controls, key hires, and reporting, in that order. I am grateful to Jack for the conviction that got Twenty One off the ground. We recently added two experienced independent directors to our Board: Paul Lalljie, a former public-company CEO and CFO, who now chairs our Audit Committee, and Karl Olsoni, with decades of financial and operational experience across energy and infrastructure, who serves on it. Second, building and acquiring operating businesses. The architecture we look to is the one Berkshire Hathaway has proven: a strong balance sheet at the center, independent operating companies around it, and disciplined capital allocation at the parent. I make that comparison with humility. Berkshire earned it over decades. We have earned nothing yet. But it is the right blueprint for what Bitcoin makes possible. If we do this well, the way people think of Berkshire and insurance, they will one day think of Twenty One and Bitcoin – strong positive cash flow. Third, developing capital-markets capabilities. Bitcoin is at once an asset to hold, collateral to lend against, and a foundation for financial products. We will use familiar tools, debt and equity, where they serve capital allocation. But where the bigger opportunity lies is in deploying new ones: instruments backed by the recurring revenues of operating businesses, at a lower cost of capital. Fourth, an M&A capability. Our industry is in a deep reset. Assets, teams, and infrastructure are repricing. For a disciplined balance sheet, this is one of the broadest opportunity sets I have seen. We have patient anchor shareholders and a public listing to deploy stock as currency. Fifth, building towards a lending and credit business. A credit market will continue to develop around Bitcoin as it establishes itself as a global monetary asset. The collateral is liquid and trades around the clock, so underwriting can lean on the collateral rather than solely on the borrower. Done conservatively, with low leverage and no shortcuts, this can be a real business, and it may extend over time to managing third-party capital. Although this will take time, it cannot mean a year of waiting. We expect to provide a fuller update later this year. In the short time I’ve been CEO, some of your initial feedback has been blunt: at the time of writing, the stock trades at a material discount to the Bitcoin we hold. That gap could be viewed as a misallocation of capital; we share that view. I also heard concerns that the build is not happening fast enough. That work has started: searches for key operating roles are underway. Ultimately, actions, not words, will address these concerns and move the company forward. I also received many questions about Tether, our controlling shareholder and an important strategic partner. Its scale, capital, and reach are real advantages, and I have built alongside its team for years, through good and bad markets. Our related-person transaction framework will remain rigorous and transparent. My early lesson at the grocery store was just the start. I also saw my family's savings frozen overnight by the government. Brazil primed me for Bitcoin. Working through the 2008 financial crisis on Wall Street pushed me the rest of the way. Bitcoin's genesis block carries a newspaper headline from January 2009: "Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks." Bitcoin is the best savings technology I have found. Its predictable monetary policy, enforced through open-source code and distributed consensus, is a major technological and social advance. Money is a memory of work, and preserving one's savings is a basic human right. One more thing. Twenty One depends on software we do not and should not control: the protocol, the wallets, the tools miners and node operators run every day. Most of it is open source, maintained by a small number of engineers with no obvious way to get paid. Expect us to do our part in strengthening that infrastructure, without strings attached. I will finish with this: Twenty One is not a substitute for Bitcoin. Investors who want pure Bitcoin exposure should understand that Bitcoin itself is the cleanest expression of that view. Twenty One must earn the right to be something different: a way to own the build around Bitcoin. That is the standard. For a long time, I ended every letter with the same three words. This industry will always throw curveballs. We do not control the next one. We control whether we keep doing the work. We keep building. Rapha Zagury Chief Executive Officer, Twenty One Capital PS: A word on communication. I am mostly a long-form person. I will communicate on X when it is useful, but I do not plan to run the company from a feed. Transparency and constant posting are not the same thing. I will write to you at least quarterly, and more often when there is something material to say. You can reach us at investors@twentyonecapital.com . We read what you send. Designed to pair one of the largest Bitcoin treasuries in the public markets with operating businesses, Twenty One aims to provide shareholders with direct, capital-efficient exposure to Bitcoin through a growing Bitcoin-native platform.
