title: Union Pacific Helps Keep Soccer Fans Moving This Summer
summary: Union Pacific Railroad worked closely with passenger rail partners during this summer’s international soccer tournament to help keep thousands of fans safely moving to and from matches across the network, including in California, Missouri, Texas and Washington.
body_text: In California, the Capitol Corridor Joint Powers Authority thanked Union Pacific for helping deliver an exceptional passenger experience during six matches in Santa Clara. With support from Union Pacific and Amtrak, Capitol Corridor carried more than 33,000 passengers on match days. In Missouri, Union Pacific partnered with Amtrak and the Missouri Department of Transportation to support increased ridership on Missouri River Runner trains connecting St. Louis and Kansas City. More than 25,000 customers traveled through Kansas City Union Station across Amtrak services during the event, contributing to an 11% increase in ridership compared to the same period last year. The tournament highlighted the close collaboration between freight railroads and passenger rail agencies, which work together every day to support safe, reliable transportation. “Our partnerships with passenger rail agencies show what's possible when we work together to meet growing transportation needs,” said Katie Novak , general director-Interline Operations, Union Pacific. “We're proud to have helped provide a safe and positive experience for travelers attending one of the world's largest sporting events.”

title: 2026 Lettuce and Jalapeño Recalls: What Restaurant Owners Should Do Now
summary: A practical restaurant response plan for the 2026 Cyclospora lettuce and Salmonella jalapeño recalls, including menu changes and supplier checks.
body_text: Last updated August 12, 2026. Restaurant owners are dealing with two major produce recalls at the same time: an iceberg lettuce recall connected to a multistate Cyclospora outbreak and a fresh jalapeño recall connected to a Salmonella outbreak. Both ingredients appear across restaurant menus, often in foods prepared in batches, including salads, tacos, burgers, salsa, pico de gallo, and guacamole. The right response is not to remove every lettuce leaf or pepper indefinitely. It is to identify affected products quickly, stop service, document what your restaurant received, clean the areas those products touched, and make temporary menu changes using ingredients from verified sources. This guide explains what restaurant owners should do now and how to keep serving customers safely while the investigations continue. What restaurant owners need to know about the 2026 recalls Iceberg lettuce recall connected to Cyclospora The FDA and CDC are investigating a Cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico and recalled by Taylor Farms de Mexico. According to the FDA's August 5 update, the outbreak included 6,358 reported illnesses in 15 states, 278 hospitalizations, and two deaths. Recalled lettuce was distributed through foodservice channels in numerous states. Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite that can cause prolonged or recurring watery diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea, fatigue, loss of appetite, and weight loss. Symptoms commonly begin about one week after exposure, although the timing can vary. Restaurants should not assume that extra washing will make affected lettuce safe. The FDA says washing may not reliably eliminate Cyclospora, and the parasite is resistant to standard chlorine-based sanitizers. Read the FDA iceberg lettuce and Cyclospora outbreak advisory. Fresh jalapeño recall connected to Salmonella The FDA is also investigating a Salmonella Javiana outbreak linked to fresh jalapeños from Sinaloa, Mexico, distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors. As of the FDA's August 10 update, the outbreak included 345 illnesses across 27 states and 36 hospitalizations, with no reported deaths. The recall covers affected fresh jalapeños supplied to wholesalers, restaurants, distributors, and foodservice companies. It has also led to downstream recalls of prepared products containing those peppers, including salsa, pico de gallo, guacamole, taco dip, burritos, sandwiches, and meat or poultry products. The FDA advises restaurants to discard affected jalapeños. If you cannot determine who supplied the peppers, work with your distributor immediately. FDA specifically advises discarding them if they came from the implicated source or if their source cannot be confirmed. Read the FDA jalapeño and Salmonella outbreak advisory. What to do in the first hour after receiving a recall notice Stop serving the ingredient. Disable affected dishes and modifiers in your POS, online ordering system, kiosks, and delivery apps. Quarantine the product. Move affected cases, containers, and prepared batches away from usable inventory. Clearly label them “Do Not Use.” Check every location. A distributor notice sent to headquarters does not guarantee every store has removed the product. Match the recall to your records. Review supplier names, invoices, receiving dates, case labels, lot codes, brands, and date markings. Identify every recipe involved. Look beyond obvious menu names. Jalapeños may be in salsa, marinades, dressings, dips, and garnishes. Iceberg lettuce may be in sandwiches, tacos, wraps, salads, bowls, and catering trays. Hold prepared batches. A salsa made with affected jalapeños remains affected even if the visible pepper pieces are removed. The same principle applies to salads and sandwich components that contacted recalled lettuce. Document the response. Record the quantities removed, affected locations, disposal or return method, cleaning completed, and the manager responsible. How to change your restaurant menu during the lettuce and jalapeño recalls A temporary menu should be smaller, easy for employees to explain, and built around ingredients whose sources you can verify. Replace or remove iceberg lettuce Serve burgers, sandwiches, and tacos without lettuce when it is not essential to the dish. Replace raw-lettuce salads with grain bowls or roasted-vegetable salads. Convert lettuce wraps into tortilla wraps, pita sandwiches, or bowls. Use cooked peppers, onions, mushrooms, or other verified ingredients to add volume and texture. Use an unaffected lettuce only after your supplier confirms the grower, processor, distributor, and relevant lot information. Replace or remove fresh jalapeños Offer pepper-free pico de gallo or guacamole. Use verified peppers from a different grower and distribution chain. Substitute cooked poblano or bell peppers from a confirmed source when the flavor profile allows. Use commercially processed hot sauce, dried chile, or chile powder for heat. Temporarily remove raw jalapeño garnishes, jalapeño cocktails, fresh salsa, and batch-made sauces when the ingredient source cannot be verified. Use a red, yellow, and green menu review Red: Items containing recalled lettuce or jalapeños. Stop selling them and discard or return the affected ingredients as directed. Yellow: Prepared foods that may contain the ingredients, shared containers, or items made on exposed equipment. Hold them until a manager verifies the recipe and handling history. Green: Dishes made with documented unaffected ingredients on cleaned equipment. These can remain available. Do not try to rescue recalled food Restaurants should not wash, trim, freeze, cook, or pickle a recalled product in an attempt to make it usable. Recall instructions call for the affected product to be discarded or returned. Cooking can reduce risks in normal food preparation, but it is not a reason to keep a recalled ingredient. House-made quick pickling should not be treated as a validated pathogen-kill step. If you need a temporary replacement, use a commercially processed product or a verified unaffected ingredient. Clean and sanitize every area the products touched After removing recalled ingredients, clean and sanitize refrigerators, produce bins, hotel pans, cutting boards, knives, food processors, prep tables, storage containers, display cases, and utensils that may have contacted them. Discard ready-to-eat foods that may have been cross-contaminated. Cleaning and sanitizing still matter even though routine chemical sanitizers may not reliably kill Cyclospora on produce. Their purpose in the restaurant response is to remove residue and reduce cross-contamination after the recalled food has been discarded. Questions to ask your produce supplier today Did our restaurant receive any product covered by either recall? What grower, processor, and distributor supplied our iceberg lettuce and jalapeños? Which delivery dates, lot codes, case labels, and locations are affected? Do any prepared products we buy contain recalled jalapeños? Can you provide written confirmation that the replacement product is from an unaffected source? How should recalled product be returned or destroyed? Who will notify us if the recall expands? Save the supplier's written response with invoices, case-label photographs, disposal records, and your internal recall log. Update every place customers can order Changing a kitchen recipe is not enough. Update menu boards, printed menus, your POS, online ordering, QR-code menus, kiosks, catering menus, and third-party delivery platforms. Remove unavailable modifiers as well as full dishes. Tell employees what changed before the next service. Give front-of-house staff a short explanation and make sure substitutions do not introduce undisclosed allergens. How to communicate with customers Keep public communication factual and specific. Do not speculate about the source or promise that no exposure occurred unless health officials have confirmed it. Due to a supplier recall, we temporarily removed certain iceberg lettuce and jalapeño products from our menu. We discarded the affected ingredients, cleaned and sanitized the areas where they were stored and prepared, and are using replacement ingredients only after verifying their source. Guests with health concerns should contact a healthcare provider and consult the current FDA advisories. What to do if an employee or customer reports symptoms Employees experiencing vomiting or diarrhea should not handle food. Follow your local health code and employee illness policy for exclusion and return-to-work requirements. Customers or employees who develop symptoms should contact a healthcare provider. Cyclospora commonly causes prolonged watery diarrhea and may require a specific stool test. Salmonella commonly causes diarrhea, fever, and abdominal cramps. Restaurant managers should cooperate promptly with state or local health departments and preserve purchase and preparation records that may assist an investigation. Restaurant recall FAQ Are all iceberg lettuce and jalapeños recalled? No. These recalls apply to particular products and supply chains. However, a restaurant should stop using an ingredient when its source cannot be established and the FDA advisory instructs operators to discard unknown-source product. Can recalled lettuce or jalapeños be washed and served? No. Recalled food should be discarded or returned according to the recall instructions. Washing does not reliably remove Cyclospora from produce, and washing is not a substitute for following a Salmonella recall. What records should a restaurant keep? Keep invoices, receiving logs, supplier communications, case labels, lot codes, delivery dates, photographs, menu recipes, disposal records, and a list of locations that received the product. When can a restaurant put the ingredient back on the menu? Resume service when your supplier can document that the replacement product is not covered by the recall and your restaurant has completed its cleaning, inventory, menu, and staff-communication steps. Build a recall plan before the next alert Every restaurant should be able to trace a high-risk ingredient from invoice to menu item within minutes. Assign one recall owner per location, retain case-label information, subscribe to FDA and local health alerts, and run a mock recall at least once a year. Your POS and online ordering tools should also make it easy to disable an ingredient, modifier, or menu item across every ordering channel. Fast menu control protects guests and prevents employees from accidentally selling an item after it has been removed in the kitchen. This article provides general operational information and is not a substitute for instructions from the FDA, CDC, your supplier, or your state or local health department.

title: Allergan Aesthetics Refreshes Allergan Partner Privileges® to Better Support Today's Modern Aesthetics Practices
summary: Updated program delivers simplified savings, greater benefits transparency, and expanded opportunities for practice growth Introduces new rewards opportunities for customer segments, including...
body_text: Updated program delivers simplified savings, greater benefits transparency, and expanded opportunities for practice growth Introduces new rewards opportunities for customer segments, including first-time APP members, growing practices, and long-standing loyal customers IRVINE, Calif. , Aug. 11, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, today announced updates to Allergan Partner Privileges® (APP), its customer portfolio loyalty program, designed to better support the way today's aesthetics practices operate and grow. Shaped by customer feedback and market momentum, the program now introduces simpler savings, greater benefits transparency and expanded opportunities for practice growth, making it easier for customers to understand, access and maximize the value of their partnership with Allergan Aesthetics. "The needs of today's aesthetics practices continue to evolve, and so should the programs designed to support them," said Nicole Mowad-Nassar, Senior Vice President, AbbVie and President, Global Allergan Aesthetics. "Our customers told us they wanted greater simplicity, more transparency and rewards that better reflect the way they operate and grow their businesses. We've invested in these program updates to create even more opportunities for our customers to realize the value of partnering with Allergan Aesthetics." Benefits That Grow with Your Practice The APP program updates are built around the areas customers cited as beneficial to running their businesses: Simplified Savings : The updated program streamlines Brand Tiers and introduces a simplified pricing discount structure designed to make savings easier to understand and access. More Allergan Aesthetics products contribute to each Brand Tier, helping customers unlock benefits sooner. Greater Transparency: Customers can now more easily see and understand their program benefits. Net pricing is clearly visible at the time of ordering and reflects savings based on loyalty benefits earned through APP status. Practices can also track APP status and upgrade progress in real time. Rewarding Growth: New Portfolio Levels reward growth across the Allergan Aesthetics portfolio and allow customers to begin earning pricing benefits sooner, based on purchasing volume. Eligible purchases across the portfolio count toward higher APP discounts, helping practices unlock greater benefits as they grow. New rewards benefits are available for specific customer segments, including first-time APP members, growing practices, and long-standing loyal customers. Additional BOTOX® Cosmetic Growth Benefit Allergan Aesthetics is also introducing a new BOTOX® Cosmetic (onabotulinumtoxinA) Growth Benefit for eligible customers that recognizes practices achieving qualifying quarterly growth by providing a quarterly rebate on eligible BOTOX® Cosmetic purchases. The Growth Benefit is designed as an additional way to support customer growth and strengthen partnership with Allergan Aesthetics. About Allergan Partner Privileges® APP is the customer portfolio loyalty program by Allergan Aesthetics designed to reward and empower aesthetics practices. Through APP, customers can earn savings, rewards, and benefits across the Allergan Aesthetics portfolio while growing their business with a trusted industry partner. About Allergan Aesthetics At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. For more information, visit www.allerganaesthetics.com . About AbbVie AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, neuroscience and oncology – and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook , Instagram , X and YouTube. Approved Uses BOTOX® Cosmetic is a prescription medicine that is injected into muscles and used to temporarily improve the look of moderate to severe forehead lines, crow's feet lines, frown lines between the eyebrows, and vertical bands connecting the jaw and neck (platysma bands) in adults. For more information, refer to the Medication Guide or talk with your doctor. To report a side effect, please call Allergan Aesthetics at 1-800-678-1605. See BOTOX® Cosmetic full Product Information , including Boxed Warning and Medication Guide . IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION BOTOX® Cosmetic may cause serious side effects that can be life threatening. Get medical help right away if you have any of these problems any time (hours to weeks) after injection of BOTOX® Cosmetic: Problems swallowing, speaking, or breathing, due to weakening of associated muscles, which can be severe and result in loss of life. You are at the highest risk if these problems are preexisting before injection. Swallowing problems may last for several months. Spread of toxin effects. The effect of botulinum toxin may affect areas away from the injection site and cause serious symptoms, including loss of strength and all-over muscle weakness, double vision, blurred vision and drooping eyelids, hoarseness or change or loss of voice, trouble saying words clearly, loss of bladder control, trouble breathing, and trouble swallowing. BOTOX ® Cosmetic dosing units are not the same as, or comparable to, any other botulinum toxin product. There has not been a confirmed serious case of spread of toxin effect when BOTOX® Cosmetic has been used at the recommended dose to treat frown lines, crow's feet lines, forehead lines, and/or platysma bands. BOTOX® Cosmetic may cause loss of strength or general muscle weakness, vision problems, or dizziness within hours to weeks of receiving BOTOX® Cosmetic. If this happens, do not drive a car, operate machinery, or do other dangerous activities. Serious and/or immediate allergic reactions have been reported, including itching, rash, red itchy welts, wheezing, asthma symptoms, or dizziness or feeling faint. Get medical help right away if you are wheezing or have asthma symptoms, or if you become dizzy or faint. Do not receive BOTOX ® Cosmetic if you are allergic to any of the ingredients in BOTOX® Cosmetic (see Medication Guide for ingredients); had an allergic reaction to any other botulinum toxin product such as Myobloc (rimabotulinumtoxinB), Dysport (abobotulinumtoxinA), Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA), Jeuveau (prabotulinumtoxinA-xvfs), Daxxify (daxibotulinumtoxinA-lanm), or Letybo (letibotulinumtoxinA-wlbg); or have a skin infection at the planned injection site. This list may not include all available botulinum toxin products. Tell your doctor about all your muscle or nerve conditions, such as ALS or Lou Gehrig's disease, myasthenia gravis, or Lambert-Eaton syndrome, as you may be at increased risk of serious side effects, including difficulty swallowing and difficulty breathing, from standard doses of BOTOX® Cosmetic. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions, including surgery or plans to have surgery on your face, trouble raising your eyebrows, drooping eyelids, any other abnormal facial change, are pregnant or plan to become pregnant (it is not known if BOTOX® Cosmetic can harm your unborn baby), or are breastfeeding or plan to (it is not known if BOTOX® Cosmetic passes into breast milk). Tell your doctor about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Using BOTOX® Cosmetic with certain other medicines may cause serious side effects. Do not start any new medicines until you have told your doctor that you have received BOTOX ® Cosmetic in the past. Tell your doctor if you have received any other botulinum toxin product in the last 4 months; have received injections of botulinum toxin such as Myobloc, Dysport, Xeomin, Jeuveau, Daxxify, or Letybo in the past (tell your doctor exactly which product you received); have recently received an antibiotic by injection; take muscle relaxants; take an allergy or cold medicine; take a sleep medicine; or take aspirin-like products or blood thinners. Other side effects of BOTOX ® Cosmetic include dry mouth; discomfort or pain at the injection site; tiredness; headache; neck pain; and eye problems, including double vision, blurred vision, decreased eyesight, drooping eyelids and eyebrows, swelling of eyelids, and dry eyes. title: Operation ASTERIX: Anatomy of a Crypto Fraud Pipeline
summary: Rapid7 Labs identified an exposed web directory on infrastructure used to support a cryptocurrency fraud operation. Raw phone-number datasets, phishing panels, voice-dialing scripts & more, alongside evidence that the operator relied on AI coding assistants throughout the campaign's development, together provide an unusual view into AI's impact on modern scams.

title: Illegal drugs seized by police from shipment of cement
summary: Illegal drugs seized by police from shipment of cement
body_text: Colombia: Officers of the Special Operations Group for Traffic and Transportation seized more than 1t of cocaine that was hidden among a shipment of cement on the Pan-American Highway. The truck was stopped for a routine inspection. Local press reports that the driver’s nervousness and the presence of several poorly sealed packages aroused officers’ suspicions, prompting them to conduct a more detailed search. Inside the vehicle, they found 34 black sacks containing 30 red packages with over 1t of cocaine hidden among cement bags. Authorities seized the 34t of cement the vehicle was carrying, as well as the truck itself and a mobile phone. "With this result, we continue to significantly impact the finances of criminal organisations dedicated to drug trafficking. Our Traffic and Transportation police maintain permanent controls on the country's main road corridors, strengthening institutional capabilities to detect new concealment methods and prevent these illicit substances from reaching their destination," said Colonel Jair Alonso Parra Archila, Director of Traffic and Transportation for the national police.

title: Rapid7 Expands UK and Ireland Channel Presence Through Strategic Partnership with Exclusive Networks
summary: Rapid7 is excited to announce a new strategic distribution partnership with Exclusive Networks across the United Kingdom and Ireland – bringing integrated security operations, trusted expertise, and partners to the region, on call to help them improve visibility and build long-term cyber resilience.
body_text: Ross Baker is Senior Director, Northern Europe at Rapid7. As organizations across the United Kingdom and Ireland embrace AI, cloud technologies, and digital transformation in the name of enhancing customer experiences and accelerating business growth, the cybersecurity landscape must continue to evolve just as quickly. In this environment, business leaders still expect security to enable innovation, not slow it down. They're pushed to reduce risk, improve visibility across expanding attack surfaces, and respond faster than ever before, with limited resources now table stakes. This is precisely why Rapid7 is excited to announce a new strategic distribution partnership with Exclusive Networks across the United Kingdom and Ireland, following previous announcements alongside the firm to better support partners across Benelux and the Nordics . Organizations no longer want disconnected security tools or transactional vendor relationships. They're looking for trusted advisors who can help simplify security operations, strengthen cyber resilience, and deliver measurable business outcomes. In this moment, cybersecurity customers are demanding experiences that create more calm. This means no more disconnected security tools or reactive approaches, but integrated security operations, trusted expertise, and partners who can help them improve visibility and build long-term cyber resilience. Investing in partner success The UK and Ireland represent one of Europe's most mature and partner-driven cybersecurity markets, with partners playing an increasingly important role in helping organizations modernize security operations for today’s AI-enabled threats. This partnership with Exclusive Networks reflects Rapid7's continued investment in the regional channel ecosystem . More than expanding distribution, it's about empowering partners with specialist expertise, technical enablement, and the go-to-market support they need to grow their cybersecurity businesses with confidence. Exclusive Networks has built an outstanding reputation as one of the UK's leading specialist cybersecurity distributors, combining deep technical expertise with a strong, partner-first approach. Together, we're creating new opportunities for partners to strengthen their capabilities while delivering greater value to customers. Helping partners deliver modern security operations Security teams are increasingly looking for platforms that unify exposure management, threat detection, response, and automation. Again we go back to the urgent need for improved visibility while reducing operational complexity. Rapid7's AI-powered cybersecurity operations platform helps organizations simplify SecOps through integrated exposure management , managed detection and response , and security automation. By bringing these capabilities together, customers can identify risk earlier, respond faster, and improve cyber resilience without adding more tools. Combined with Exclusive Networks' technical enablement, solution engineering expertise, and established channel ecosystem, this new alliance makes it easier for partners to deliver integrated cybersecurity solutions while expanding managed security services and fostering long-term customer relationships. Looking ahead Rapid7 and Exclusive Networks share a common commitment to helping partners grow through technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous enablement. Together, we're investing in the resources, expertise, and support needed to help partners succeed in one of Europe's most dynamic cybersecurity markets. Ready to grow with Rapid7? Head to our Partners page for more news, resources, and opportunities.

title: Everything You Wanted to Know Before Your First Day as a Marriott Intern
summary: Starting a Marriott internship? Interns share what to wear, how to prepare, questions to ask, and advice to make the most of day one.
body_text: Starting an internship can come with a lot of tiny questions that feel surprisingly big: What should I wear? How should I prepare? What will meetings be like? Who do I ask if I’m confused? The good news? You don’t have to figure it out on your own. We asked Emeline, an HQ Fellow, and Lynn, a summer intern at the Hotel Arts Barcelona, a Ritz-Carlton property, all your burning questions. From what to wear on day one to what to research, and they had a lot to say. → Thinking about beginning your own Marriott journey? Explore where your path could begin Why Marriott Emeline: Growing up in the Bethesda area, I had always passed by the Marriott HQ building. I thought it was so cool that the world’s largest hospitality company was located in my hometown. As soon as I was eligible to apply to Marriott’s Fellowship program, it was a no-brainer. Lynn: I have always been passionate about hospitality, but I didn’t just want to work in any hotel. I wanted to experience what true luxury hospitality looks like behind the scenes. Also, Marriott has an outstanding reputation worldwide. Courtesy of Emeline V. What to do before day one Emeline: I looked up ‘ Marriott HQ Office Tour’ on YouTube, excited to see what the building I would be working at every day had in store! Lynn: I researched Marriott International, The Ritz-Carlton, and Hotel Arts Barcelona. I read about Marriott’s service philosophy, guest satisfaction, and The Ritz-Carlton Gold Standards. I also looked at guest reviews, photos of the hotel, and videos online. What to wear and what not to overthink Emeline: Preparing for the first day, another Fellow and I were texting different outfits back and forth. Since this was my first time wearing “business casual”, I also did a lot of TikTok research on what that looks like. I ended up wearing black slacks and a black blouse! Thanks for your help, Ava! Lynn: I probably spent way too much time thinking about what to wear. I remember trying different outfits and asking myself, ‘Is this formal enough? Or maybe it’s too formal?’ Eventually, I chose a professional business outfit. When I arrived at the Hotel Arts Barcelona, a Ritz-Carlton property, I immediately realized I had made the right choice. Courtesy of Lynn N. What the first week really looks like Emeline: I had a little bit of imposter syndrome. I was also nervous about meeting all the other Fellows and my team, but everyone was so welcoming! Marriott has a department for almost everything and hires people of all different majors! You don’t have to be a hospitality major (and I’m not!) to work here. There are people doing law, finance, design, technology, etc. No matter what you study or what you’re interested in, there is a job for you. Lynn: The biggest surprise was how genuinely welcoming everyone was, taking the time to introduce themselves, answer my questions, and help me whenever I needed it. I was also surprised by how much teamwork and attention to detail happen behind the scenes. Guests only see the final experience, but there are so many small gestures that might seem insignificant but can completely change a guest’s experience. Best questions to ask your mentor, manager or team Emeline: “Who are two more people you think I should talk to? Can you introduce me?” My mentor (a past Fellow himself) gave me the idea of asking this question, and it has led to some great connections! Lynn: One of the best questions I asked was whether I could become involved in projects and activities beyond my daily responsibilities. Because I asked, I had the opportunity to participate in incredibly exciting initiatives that taught me much more than if I had only completed my daily tasks. They made my internship much more valuable. Courtesy of Emeline V. What I’d text my pre-internship self Emeline: Say yes to everything: Fellow lunches, a project, joining the meeting, running the errand. Be the person people can depend on. It goes by fast, so really lean into these 10 weeks! Lynn: There will be days when you doubt yourself, feel overwhelmed, or think you’re not good enough–but don’t listen to those thoughts. Trust yourself, ask questions, say yes to every opportunity, and never be afraid to step outside your comfort zone. Every challenge will help you grow into a stronger, more confident version of yourself. Enjoy every moment, because before you know it, you’ll look back with pride at everything you’ve achieved. → Ready to take the next step? Explore Marriott Early Careers

title: Is LinkedIn Even Worth It? An Honest Reality-Check (2026)
summary: LinkedIn is two products in one: a searchable resume recruiters actually use, and a feed you can skip. Here is the honest, low-effort version worth having.
body_text: Is LinkedIn actually worth your time in 2026? Mostly yes, but only for a narrow slice of what it does. Recruiters really do search it to find people, so a complete, findable profile pays off even while you sit still. The feed is a different animal: humble-brags, guru grift, and AI-written motivation you can skip entirely. Treat LinkedIn as a searchable resume that works in the background, not a stage you have to perform on. Set it up well, mark yourself open to recruiters, and then largely leave it alone. That is the version worth having. Ask a room of job seekers whether LinkedIn is worth it and you will get two answers, both loud, both partly right. One camp swears it landed them their last three jobs. The other calls it a corporate cesspool of flexing and platitudes and wants nothing to do with it. The strange thing is that these people are describing the same website. They are just using different parts of it. That is the whole trick to answering the question honestly. LinkedIn is really two products wearing one logo. One is a giant, heavily-used database of searchable professional profiles that recruiters pay real money to dig through. The other is a social feed that has drifted somewhere between a networking event and Instagram for people who wear lanyards to brunch. The database half is genuinely useful. The feed half is mostly noise you are free to ignore. Almost every argument about whether LinkedIn is "worth it" collapses the moment you stop treating it as one thing. So this is not a "delete it" piece, and it is definitely not a "become an influencer" piece. It is a reality-check on which parts earn their keep, which parts you can wave off, and how little effort the useful version actually takes. The honest answer, up front Worth having a solid, findable profile. Not worth the performance treadmill. Use it as a utility, not a stage. That is the short version, and most of the people who have thought about this hard end up somewhere close to it. The value sits almost entirely in being searchable and being reachable. A recruiter who can find you, and can tell in a glance that you are a real person with real experience, is the payoff. Everything downstream of that (the posting, the commenting, the reacting to a stranger's promotion) is optional at best and a time sink at worst. Here is the honest part people skip: being absent has a cost too. In most white-collar, corporate, and tech-adjacent fields, a hiring manager or recruiter who looks you up and finds nothing reads that as a small red flag. Not disqualifying. Just a shrug where a nod should have been. So the question was never really "should I be on LinkedIn," it was "how much of it do I actually have to touch." The answer to that is: a lot less than the platform wants you to believe. What it is genuinely good for Strip away the hype and there is a real, defensible case for LinkedIn. It rests on four things, none of which require you to post a single word. Recruiters search it to source candidates. This is the load-bearing fact, and it is the one people are wrong about most often. Recruiters, especially in-house recruiters working a specific req, live inside the search tool. They run keyword and skills queries, and they pull up profiles that match. When a recruiter reaches out with a specific, well-targeted message rather than a copy-paste blast, that is the machine working the way it is supposed to. People overhaul a stale profile and then hear from a recruiter a few weeks later, and it does not feel like coincidence because it usually is not. If nobody is finding you, the culprit is almost never that recruiters left the platform. It is that you are not surfacing in their searches, which is a fixable problem. We dug into exactly why in why no recruiters message you on LinkedIn . Referrals and warm intros. The blunt reality of hiring is that a referral will beat a cold application most days of the week, and LinkedIn is where those loose ties stay warm. The classmate who moved to a company you want, the former manager two jobs back, the person you sat next to on a project for six months: those connections are worth keeping findable, because one of them being able to vouch for you is worth more than fifty applications shouted into the void. You do not have to network in the cringe-inducing, "let's grab a virtual coffee" sense. You just have to be connected to the people you have actually worked with, so a warm path exists when you need it. Passive discovery while you are not looking. This might be the single highest-return use of the whole platform, and it costs you nothing after setup. A findable, current profile means opportunities can come to you even when you are happily employed and not searching. Some of the best jobs people land arrive as an unsolicited message about a company they had never heard of. You cannot get that message if you are invisible. Being quietly open to hearing about roles is a lever you control, and we covered how to pull it without lighting a flare in does the Open to Work badge hurt you . A findable professional presence. When someone is deciding whether to interview you, they often look you up. A complete profile that lines up with your resume corroborates that you are who you say you are. Endorsements and a real work history nudge the reader toward believing the document in front of them. An empty or contradictory profile does the opposite. This is quiet, unglamorous, and it matters. Add those up and, for most corporate, tech, and knowledge-work roles, a solid profile lands somewhere close to table stakes. Not because a rule says so, but because that is where the people who make hiring decisions go to check. Would a recruiter actually find you? Get a free, section-by-section read on whether your profile is searchable, complete, and saying the right things to the people who source there. Review my LinkedIn → What it is overrated and insufferable for Now the counterweight, and it deserves to be said plainly rather than tucked into a footnote. A large amount of what makes LinkedIn feel exhausting is real, and none of it is the part that helps you get hired. The feed has drifted into influencer territory. Motivational stories engineered for reach, screenshots of rejection turned into a five-act redemption arc, the "Question? Answer." broetry format where every sentence gets its own line for gravity it did not earn. It reads like a professional version of Instagram, except everyone is performing for their boss instead of their friends. You are allowed to find this insufferable. Plenty of people who use LinkedIn every single day for the useful stuff cannot stand the feed and simply do not scroll it. Then there is the announcement theater. The "humbled and honored" posts, the awards nobody has heard of presented as milestones, the job-title field that has quietly become first-person fan fiction where a cashier becomes a "customer experience professional at an industry-leading organization." Some of this is harmless. Some of it is a status game dressed up as authenticity. Either way, none of it is a requirement, and treating it as one is how the platform makes you miserable. The guru economy is the loudest offense. If a stranger's profile calls them a guru, a ninja, or a thought leader, that is usually the tell that they are selling something. The whole genre of hustle content, the "DM me to change your life" grift, the coding hot take engineered purely to farm engagement: you can scroll past all of it and lose nothing. If you want the fuller taxonomy of the exact phrases recruiters glaze over, we cataloged them in the LinkedIn buzzwords recruiters skip right past . And a fair chunk of the feed is now written by a machine. AI-generated posts, AI-polished profiles that all read in the same faintly hollow register, the same three emoji, the same faux-vulnerable opener. The backlash to that is real, and it is a genuine question whether leaning on AI for your own profile helps or hurts. We got into that in the AI-slop LinkedIn backlash . The short of it: the tool is fine, the tell is when it does the thinking for you. Here is the mercy in all of this. Every single thing in this section lives in the feed. None of it lives in the database. You can have the useful half without touching any of the exhausting half, and that is not some clever workaround, it is just how the thing was built. Do you actually need it? This is where honest advice has to admit it depends, because it does. There is no rule that everyone must be on LinkedIn, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something. The strongest case for needing it is field-driven. If you work in corporate, tech, or knowledge work, the answer leans hard toward yes. That is where recruiters source, where hiring managers check, and where a decent profile is close to assumed. If you are early in your career and doing all the searching yourself, it matters less day to day, but it still pays to have the profile built out for later, when you would rather be found than hunt. The case for needing it far less is also real. Trades, local service work, owner-operators, and fields that hire almost entirely through word of mouth or a referral network genuinely get less out of it. If your next job comes from a phone call, a jobsite reputation, or a regular who knows a guy, LinkedIn is a nice-to-have at most. Some very capable people run whole businesses and avoid it on principle, and they are not wrong to. So the useful way to decide is not "is LinkedIn worth it" in the abstract. It is: how does hiring actually happen in my corner of the world? If the answer runs through recruiters, ATS pipelines, and formal applications, a profile earns its keep. If it runs through people who already know your work, it matters far less. We mapped the whole apply-to-offer machine, and where LinkedIn sits inside it, in how hiring actually works . One more thing worth saying: even the reluctant tend to keep a bare profile alive, just in case. That instinct is sound. The cost of having one is close to zero once it exists. The cost of building one from scratch the week you suddenly need it is a scramble at the worst possible time. The minimal-effort LinkedIn If the last two sections landed as "the good stuff is real but the rest is a drain," good. That is the setup for the actual payoff, which is that you can capture most of the value for a fraction of the effort. You do not have to be an influencer, you do not have to post, and honestly you barely have to log in. Here is the version for people who find the whole thing tiresome. Build it once, tune a few fields, then leave it running in the background like a smoke detector. Complete the profile honestly. Real roles, real dates, real responsibilities. A profile that lines up with your resume does the corroboration work quietly. Gaps and contradictions do the opposite. Write a headline that leads with what you do. Your headline is the most searchable, most-seen line you have, and on mobile a recruiter often sees only the first few words. Put the job title first. Save the personality for later, if at all. If you want the full breakdown of what to keep and what to cut, the buzzword guide covers it. Fill the skills section like it is a search index, because it is. A lot of recruiters search on skills alone. If the skill they are hunting is not listed, you do not appear. This is the least glamorous field on the whole profile and one of the most important. Use a decent photo. Not a glamour shot. Just clear, recent, and human. It is a small lever with an outsized effect on whether a stranger trusts the profile, and we broke down exactly what reads well in your LinkedIn photo is costing you recruiter replies . Set yourself open to recruiters only. You can signal availability to the people searching without slapping the public green banner on your face for your current boss to see. That quieter setting does most of the work with none of the exposure. The full trade-off is in the Open to Work explainer . That is the entire program. Five things, done once, revisited when your title changes or when you decide to start looking. No daily posting, no engagement farming, no reacting to a former colleague's fifth "grateful and humbled" announcement of the quarter. The database does the work while you get on with your life. If you want a second set of eyes on whether your profile is actually pulling its weight, a quick LinkedIn review will flag the searchable fields you left thin and the phrases that make a recruiter's eyes slide right past. If you are wary of it: staying in control A real objection to LinkedIn has nothing to do with cringe and everything to do with control. What is it collecting, who can see what I am doing, and can my current employer tell I am poking around. These are reasonable worries, and the good news is that using LinkedIn minimally does not mean surrendering the wheel. You can browse without broadcasting. There is a private-viewing setting, though it is worth knowing exactly how private it really is before you rely on it, which we picked apart in whether LinkedIn private mode is actually private . You can also control the panic that goes the other way, the fear that a recruiter can somehow see every job you deleted or every move you made. Mostly they cannot, and the real leak is duller than the myth, which we walked through in whether recruiters can see the jobs you deleted . And if the thing keeping you up at night is your data feeding an AI model, there is a toggle for that, and deleting your account is usually the wrong move for the wrong reason. We laid out what is actually happening and how to opt out in should you delete LinkedIn before it trains AI on you . The point across all three: you can benefit from being findable without being "on" the platform in any exhausting sense, and you can keep a firm hand on what you share and who sees it. The "LinkedIn is dead" claim is exaggerated Every year or so a wave of posts declares LinkedIn dead, drowning in AI, useless for actual hiring. The feed being worse than it used to be is true. The platform being useless is not, and the two get conflated constantly. The database is not dead. Recruiters still open it every morning and search it. People still get hired off unsolicited messages. Referrals still route through it. What people usually mean when they say it feels dead is that the feed got insufferable and their own inbox went quiet, and the second part almost always traces back to searchability rather than a mass recruiter exodus. If your messages dried up, the fix is in your profile, not in a eulogy for the site. There is a viral genre of "I worked at LinkedIn, here is the secret truth" posts that muddies this further, and a lot of it does not survive contact with people who actually run the tool. We audited the biggest ones in the ex-LinkedIn-employee myth audit . Skepticism is healthy. Just aim it at the right target. A word on applying through LinkedIn One narrow tactical note, because it comes up constantly. Being findable on LinkedIn and applying to jobs through LinkedIn are two different activities, and they deserve different levels of enthusiasm. Findability is the crown jewel, and applying through the site is more of a mixed bag. The one-click Easy Apply flow is convenient, but it also produces a flood of low-effort applications, and a lot of people prefer to find the posting on LinkedIn and then apply on the company's own careers page instead. Recruiters on the receiving end tend to skim the parsed history and read your actual resume anyway, so the polish of your submission matters more than the channel. And the intimidating "over 100 applicants" counter is far less meaningful than it looks, partly because a chunk of those "applicants" are just clicks. We unpacked that number in what over 100 applicants really means . If you do want to use LinkedIn as a search engine for openings, the practical how-to guide covers the mechanics. The verdict So, is LinkedIn even worth it? For most people in most professional fields, yes, but only in the specific, boring, low-effort way that actually matters. Worth a complete, findable profile that lets recruiters source you and lets warm ties vouch for you. Worth the fifteen minutes it takes to lead with your job title, fill the skills, add a real photo, and flag yourself open to recruiters. Worth having in the background even when you are not looking, precisely because that is when the good messages tend to arrive. Not worth the anxiety. Not worth the comparison to a feed full of other people's best-day-ever posts. Not worth the pressure to become a personal brand, to post through your feelings, or to react to strangers' promotions in the hope the algorithm smiles on you. That whole layer is optional, and opting out of it costs you nothing that helps you get hired. Use it as a tool, not a stage. Set it up well, keep it honest, and then go live your life. The version of LinkedIn that is worth it is the one you barely have to think about. Frequently Asked Questions Do I really need LinkedIn to get a job? Depends on your field. For corporate, tech, and knowledge work, a solid profile is close to expected because that is where recruiters search and hiring managers check. For trades, local service work, and referral-driven fields, it matters much less. Ask how hiring happens in your corner of the world, then decide. Is LinkedIn actually dead in 2026? The feed is worse than it used to be. The database is not dead at all. Recruiters still search it daily and people still get hired off unsolicited messages. When it feels dead, that usually means your inbox went quiet, which almost always traces back to a searchability problem , not a recruiter exodus. Do I have to post on LinkedIn to get value from it? No. This is the biggest misconception. Almost all of the hiring value comes from being findable and reachable, which requires zero posting. You can build a strong profile, set yourself open to recruiters, and never write a single update. Posting is optional, and for most people it is skippable. Why does everyone say LinkedIn is toxic? Because the feed can be. Humble-brags, guru grift, and performance-as-authenticity are real and grating. But that is one half of the platform. The searchable-profile half, the part that actually helps you get hired, has none of that in it. You can use the useful half and never scroll the feed. What is the minimum I should do on LinkedIn? Five things. Complete the profile honestly, lead your headline with your job title, fill the skills section, add a clear recent photo, and set yourself open to recruiters only. Do that once, revisit it when your title changes, and you have captured most of the value for very little effort. Do recruiters actually find people through LinkedIn? Yes, constantly, especially in-house recruiters working a specific role. They run keyword and skills searches and reach out to matches. If nobody is finding you, it is rarely that recruiters left. It is usually that you are not surfacing in their searches, which you can fix by tuning your profile for search . Should I use the public Open to Work banner? Not necessarily. You can signal availability to recruiters only, which does most of the work without your current employer seeing a green banner on your photo. The full trade-off between the two settings is in the Open to Work explainer . Can my employer tell I am job hunting on LinkedIn? Mostly not, if you use the private settings and the recruiters-only availability option. There is a private-viewing mode, though it has limits worth understanding first. We covered exactly how private it is in the private mode breakdown . Is it worth using AI to write my LinkedIn profile? The tool is fine as an assist. The trouble starts when it does the thinking and every profile ends up in the same hollow register recruiters have learned to spot. Use it to tighten, not to invent. The fuller picture is in the AI-slop breakdown . Should I apply to jobs through LinkedIn or the company site? Being findable on LinkedIn matters more than applying through it. Easy Apply is convenient but noisy, so many people find the posting on LinkedIn and apply on the company's careers page instead. And the "over 100 applicants" counter is less meaningful than it looks, as we explain in this piece on applicant counts . title: How to Locate Faults in Low-Voltage Utility Systems — MSC Industrial Supply Co.
summary: In utility systems, locating faults quickly and accurately is crucial to minimize downtime and ensure the safety of the electrical infrastructure.
body_text: In utility systems, locating faults quickly and accurately is crucial to minimize downtime and ensure the safety and reliability of the electrical infrastructure. Faults such as shorts, opens, and ground faults can disrupt operations and pose significant risks. A wire tracer is an essential tool for identifying and locating these faults in low-voltage systems up to 600V AC. This application note provides a step-by-step guide for using a wire tracer to locate faults in low-voltage utility systems, ensuring efficient and effective fault resolution. Scenario: Locating Faults in a Utility Substation You are tasked with locating faults in low-voltage cables at a utility substation where intermittent power outages and equipment failures have been reported. The substation has an extensive network of low-voltage cables, and accurate fault location is critical for restoring reliable service. Using a wire tracer will help you quickly identify and locate the faults. Tools Needed Fluke 2062 Advanced Pro Wire Tracer Kit (CAT IV 600 V, with i400 AC Current Clamp) Insulation resistance tester Voltage tester (optional) Multimeter Screwdriver Insulated gloves and protective gear Circuit labels Notebook or digital device for documentation Read more: Get Started with the Right Multimeter and Clamp Meter Pairing Step-by-Step Guide to Wire Tracer Fault Location in Low-Voltage Utility Systems Step 1: Investigate and Secure Discuss with Utility Management: Gather information about the reported issues, including affected areas and any recent changes to the low-voltage system. Discuss the project scope with utility management. Safety First: Inform relevant personnel about the scheduled fault location work. Follow all safety protocols, including wearing insulated gloves and other protective gear. Step 2: Prepare the Tracer Prepare the Transmitter: Connect the transmitter to the cable suspected of having a fault. Ensure it is properly connected (follow set-up instructions in user’s manual to refresh your knowledge). And follow safety procedures for low-voltage connections. Activate the Receiver: Move to the electrical panel or designated area with the receiver. Turn it on and set it to the appropriate mode to detect the transmitter signal. Step 3: Trace the Low-Voltage Cables Scan the Cable Path: Slowly move the receiver along the path of the low-voltage cable. The receiver will pick up the signal from the transmitter, allowing you to trace the cable's route. Identify Fault Locations: Pay attention to changes in the signal strength. A sudden drop in the signal may indicate an open circuit or break. Mark the location. To verify the location of fault, move the transmitter to the other end of the wire and repeat tracing steps from the opposite end. If the signal drops at the same location, the fault has been located. Document the Path: As you trace the cable path, document the route and potential fault locations. Use a notebook or digital device to record the information, which will be valuable for future maintenance and troubleshooting. Step 4: Verify Faults Turn Off Power: Before accessing any low-voltage connections, turn off the power to the affected cable. Use a voltage tester to confirm the power is off. Inspect the Cables: Open junction boxes and inspect the cables at the identified fault locations. Look for signs of damage, wear, or loose connections. Test with Insulation Resistance Tester: Use an insulation resistance tester to check for insulation breakdown and verify the integrity of the cables. This step ensures the cables are in good condition. Step 5: Repair Faults Fix Loose Connections: Tighten any loose connections and ensure all connections are properly secured. Repair or Replace Damaged Cables: If damaged cables are found, repair them using appropriate insulation materials or replace the faulty section with new cable. Secure Connections: Ensure all connections are properly insulated and secured according to low-voltage safety standards. Step 6: Test and Verify Reassemble Junction Boxes: Once all inspections and repairs are complete, reassemble the junction boxes and secure all covers. Restore Power: Turn the power back on at the control panel. Use a voltage tester to verify that power is restored to the cables. Test the System: Use the wire tracer to verify that there are no remaining issues. Perform a thorough test to ensure the reliability and safety of the low-voltage system. Troubleshooting Table Issue Solution Weak Signal from Receiver Ensure the transmitter is properly connected, check the batteries, and verify connections Multiple Faults Detected Address each fault one at a time, starting with the most critical or accessible one Persistent Faults Use additional testing equipment such as insulation resistance testers to identify deeper issues Practical Tips for Effective Fault Location Use Clear Labeling: Clearly label each cable, junction box, and connection point to avoid confusion and ensure a smooth fault location process. Keep Detailed Records: Document all findings, including the locations and types of faults found and addressed. This information is essential for future reference and planning. Double-Check Repairs: After making repairs, double-check all connections to ensure they are secure and meet safety standards. Regular Inspections: Schedule regular inspections of cables and connections to identify and address potential issues before they become significant problems. Conclusion Using a wire tracer for locating faults in low-voltage utility systems is essential for ensuring the safety, reliability, and efficiency of electrical infrastructure. By following the steps outlined in this application note, you can quickly and accurately locate faults, perform necessary repairs, and ensure the continued safe operation of critical electrical systems. Investing in a high-quality wire tracer, such as the Fluke 2062 Advanced Pro Wire Tracer Kit, can significantly enhance your ability to perform professional and reliable electrical maintenance services. This article was previously featured on Fluke's blog .

title: InterContinental Hotels & Resorts Celebrates 80 Years with 'DOORS UNLOCKED' in Greater China
summary: 6 August 2026, Shanghai – InterContinental Hotels & Resorts, a flagship brand within IHG Hotels & Resorts' Luxury & Lifestyle portfolio, today announced the launch of 'DOORS UNLOCKED' in Greater China to mark its 80th anniversary. The programme offers a series of exclusive, theatre-led cultural experiences in key cities, including Beijing and Shanghai.
body_text: News releases 11 August 2026 InterContinental Hotels & Resorts Celebrates 80 Years with 'DOORS UNLOCKED' in Greater China 11 August 2026, Shanghai – InterContinental Hotels & Resorts, a flagship brand within IHG Hotels & Resorts' Luxury & Lifestyle portfolio, today announced the launch of 'DOORS UNLOCKED' in Greater China to mark its 80th anniversary. The programme offers a series of exclusive, theatre-led cultural experiences in key cities, including Beijing and Shanghai. Created in collaboration with premier performing arts institutions in Greater China, 'DOORS UNLOCKED' blends exclusive performances and backstage access with curated hotel stays. The initiative aims to provide guests with a deeper, more meaningful cultural immersion— opening doors to a world of fascination . IHG Hotels & Resorts Greater China leadership and guests at InterContinental Hotels & Resorts’ 80th anniversary celebration download " For 80 years, InterContinental has been helping guests see the world from new perspectives, " said Rita Jiang, Chief Commercial & Marketing Officer, Greater China, IHG Hotels & Resorts . " We believe luxury is defined not just by the quality of a stay, but by the connections and memories a journey creates. 'DOORS UNLOCKED' builds on this belief by combining our insider expertise with the creativity of leading cultural institutions, offering a more engaging way to experience each city through its stories and stages. " Immersive theatre experience at the brand’s anniversary celebration download Unlocking Each City through Performing Arts InterContinental Hotels & Resorts continues to deepen its core brand philosophy while exploring cross-cultural integration. On August 5, the brand's anniversary celebration at InterContinental Beijing Sanlitun featured an exclusive immersive theatre performance by artists from six national arts troupes, alongside a roundtable dialogue with five "InterContinental Insiders" and industry leaders—vividly bringing to life the hotel's role as a "city cultural living room." Meanwhile, InterContinental Hotels & Resorts is collaborating with Beijing Tianqiao Performing Arts Center, Shanghai Culture Square and other arts institutions. The programme will launch in August with theatre-led experiences in Beijing and Shanghai first, pairing selected productions with curated stays and tailored privileges at participating InterContinental hotels. Further collaborations will be introduced in phases. By connecting the stage with the stay, DOORS UNLOCKED extends cultural discovery beyond the theatre, offering guests an insider’s perspective on the cities they visit.
